courseContributions.ACCPPDE101: Mandatory Year-1 personal/professional development and academic skills.
courseContributions.BENBUSI112: Financial statements and annual-report analysis explain firm information used in economic and business decisions; not a substitute for CAPM, portfolio pricing or advanced corporate finance.
courseContributions.BENBUSI211: AI business cases analyse effects on competition, labour, growth, inequality and corporate governance; an economic application, not a technical AI-methods course.
courseContributions.BENBUSI312: Applied budgeting, investment and risk decisions add a financial-decision application to macroeconomic and firm analysis; no dedicated asset-pricing or financial-stability sequence is claimed.
courseContributions.BENECON111: Supply/demand, consumer and firm theory, market structures and short-run macroeconomics establish economic foundations.
courseContributions.BENECON211: Growth, inflation, unemployment, fiscal/monetary policy, business cycles and trade support economic-policy analysis; not a duplicate of VU’s specialised intermediate policy course.
courseContributions.BENECON212: Uncertainty, behavioural preferences, imperfect competition, factor markets, equilibrium and externalities implement intermediate microeconomic analysis after statistical foundations.
courseContributions.BENECON311: Market failure, public goods, taxation, spending and redistribution directly implement public-welfare and policy analysis.
courseContributions.BENECON312: OLS/GLS/instrumental variables, sampling distributions, tests and an empirical economic paper provide applied econometric research; VU Probit/panel/time-series coverage is not assumed.
courseContributions.BENECON314: Experiments, biases, heuristics and framing explain deviations from conventional economic choice and support consumer or policy interpretation.
courseContributions.BENENTR111: Customer interviews, needs-to-product translation, cost/proceeds and sustainable prototypes implement consumer-led market validation, not generic design breadth.
courseContributions.BENENTR211: Consumer psychology, brand trust, marketing plans and strategy implement the evidenced consumer/marketing direction.
courseContributions.BENENTR212: Business-model analysis, digital-value opportunities and a strategic plan implement responsible digital business strategy.
courseContributions.BENENTR311: Collecting and analysing customer evidence and communicating findings provide market-research practice complementary to econometric methods.
courseContributions.BENENTR312: Institutional, political and cultural forces, trade and corporate responsibility explain the conditions under which firms make cross-border economic decisions.
courseContributions.BENGATE101: Venture ideation, customer validation and business planning implement the target’s entrepreneurship and firm-decision strand.
courseContributions.BENGATE102: Operationalisation, sampling, experimental design, inference, ANOVA and a group project establish empirical research before Microeconomics and advanced work.
courseContributions.BENLEAD311: Motivation, decision making, leadership, group dynamics and organisational structure explain workplace behaviour; not formal organisational economics.
courseContributions.BENLEAD312: BATNA/ZOPA, bargaining, trade-offs and simulations implement consumer/business negotiation and strategic interpersonal decisions, not market-equilibrium theory.
courseContributions.DISDATA111: Data cleaning, visualisation and manipulation support reproducible economic/consumer evidence and project work.
courseContributions.DISDATA211: Regression, classification, resampling, shrinkage, trees and clustering support predictive analysis of economic/consumer data; causal inference remains the econometrics contribution.
courseContributions.DISGATE101: Python programming and debugging implement computational tools for digital business and empirical projects.
courseContributions.DISGATE102: Calculus, integration and differential equations give mathematical tools for economic modelling; no unsupported linear-algebra/linear-programming claim.
courseContributions.DISMATH213: Numerical roots, interpolation, differentiation/integration and differential equations support quantitative model solution; not a dedicated optimisation course.
courseContributions.DISMATH314: Probability distributions, estimation, sampling and simulation provide a mathematical basis for empirical economic inference.
courseContributions.ENSSUST111: Physical climate drivers, social impacts, mitigation and adaptation constrain economic climate-policy choices; not an environmental/transport-economics replacement.
courseContributions.GOSPHIL212: Moral theories and applied equality, future-generation and climate questions support evaluation of welfare-policy judgments; not VU’s dedicated corporate/market-ethics scope.
courseContributions.GOSPOLI311: EU institutions, legislative dossiers, interest groups and transparency data explain the political institutions shaping economic policy, not technical economic-policy models.

FinanceShortfall: Banking/financial decisions retained in primary; no independent specialistFinance option from accounting+generaldiscrete/linear maths+businesslaw. Public Economics, climate, ethics versus consumer design/negotiation/digitalstrategy/programming are a genuine curricular priority shift.
